title: Learning and Editing Universal Graph Prompt Tuning via Reinforcement Learning

problem.claim: Graph prompt tuning must bridge general graph representations and task-specific requirements across downstream tasks.

gap.claim: Selective node-based graph prompt tuning is argued to compromise the theoretical foundation of universal graph prompt tuning.

contributions.claim: The paper strengthens the theoretical foundation of universal graph prompt tuning by imposing stricter constraints and showing that adding prompts to all nodes is necessary for universality.
LEAP combines basic universal graph prompts with actor-critic reinforcement learning to select nodes and edit prompts.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors introduce the novel LEAP model and paradigm for preserving universal graph prompt tuning's theoretical foundation while pursuing more ideal prompts.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Across graph- and node-level tasks, varied pre-training strategies, and full-shot and few-shot settings, LEAP consistently outperforms fine-tuning and other prompt-based approaches.

narrative_sequence.summary: Pre-training and prompt-tuning has become important for improving graph representation learning across downstream tasks.
Graph prompt tuning uses pre-trained models and task-specific prompts to connect general representations with task requirements.
Task-specific approaches limit adaptability, while selective node-based approaches are argued to undermine universal prompt tuning's theoretical basis.
The paper strengthens universality constraints and introduces LEAP, which selects nodes and edits universal prompts using actor-critic reinforcement learning.
The authors report consistent performance gains over fine-tuning and other prompt-based methods across tasks, pre-training strategies, and shot settings.

source_observation.claim: The method preserves universal graph prompts while using reinforcement learning to select nodes and edit prompts.

interpretation.claim: A principled universal representation can be combined with adaptive prompt optimization.

application.claim: When designing adaptable graph prompt systems, preserve the conditions supporting universality while optimizing prompt placement and content.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the reported approach generalizes beyond the evaluated tasks, strategies, and shot settings.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the reinforcement-learning state, action, reward, or training procedure.
The abstract does not identify datasets, baselines, numerical results, or statistical significance.
The abstract does not provide details of the stricter theoretical constraints or proof.
